calls.reason: The SWE-CI preprint finds newer models in each family always scored higher. GAO's Patriot report and the Therac-25 investigation tie deaths to software errors in critical systems, so both parts held.

Established literature, as summarized in the SWE-CI preprint, puts maintenance at 60-80% of lifecycle cost and says quality degrades over time (Lehman's laws). That fits maintenance being the bigger, harder task, though the source is secondhand.
This forecast has no deadline. The EASE 2026 study, with humans doing about 83% of maintenance on AI-written files, fits it so far but cannot settle it.

Amazon's internal note, as reported by the FT, named GenAI-assisted changes as a factor. Amazon says publicly only one incident involved AI tooling and none involved AI-written code, and calls the Kiro disruption limited. No neutral post-mortem settles how big the AI-linked problems were.
